t: Effective with respect to appropriations for fiscal years ending after June 30, 1968, section 1 (b) (1) of the Vocational Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. 31(b)(1)) is amended by striking out “and”, and by inserting before the period at the end thereof for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969, the sum of $500,000,000, and for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970, the sum of $600,000,000”.

fable.w: This section only amends the Vocational Rehabilitation Act to set authorized appropriation amounts for fiscal years 1969 and 1970. A tempting reading is that vocational rehabilitation funding implies grants to and coordination with states, but nothing in the text calls for consultation, hearings, rulemaking, advisory bodies, or any right to sue. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision here.
fable.s: for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969, the sum of $500,000,000, and for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970, the sum of $600,000,000

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations provision that authorizes specific funding amounts for the Vocational Rehabilitation Act. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or requirements for state/local input mentioned in this text.
qwen_block.s: Effective with respect to appropriations for fiscal years ending after June 30, 1968, section 1 (b) (1) of the Vocational Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. 31(b)(1)) is amended by striking out “and”, and by inserting before the period at the end thereof for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969, the sum of $500,000,000, and for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970, the sum of $600,000,000”.

opus.w: The section only raises the funding amounts in the Vocational Rehabilitation Act to $500,000,000 for fiscal year 1969 and $600,000,000 for fiscal year 1970. It provides no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue. Mentioning a law about state programs does not bring outside parties into any federal decision.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking.** One could misread this as participation because it amends the Vocational Rehabilitation Act, which deals with state programs. But the amendment only changes the authorized dollar amounts for fiscal years 1969 and 1970. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, asked to comment, put on an advisory body or given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a pure appropriation amendment that sets specific funding levels for the Vocational Rehabilitation Act for certain fiscal years. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The definition of participation requires interaction with parties outside the federal government before a decision is made, which is absent here.
qwen_chat.s: Effective with respect to appropriations for fiscal years ending after June 30, 1968, section 1 (b) (1) of the Vocational Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. 31(b)(1)) is amended by striking out “and”, and by inserting before the period at the end thereof for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969, the sum of $500,000,000, and for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970, the sum of $600,000,000”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that because the text amends a statute related to vocational rehabilitation, it involves public participation or grants. However, the text itself is purely an appropriation amendment, specifying dollar amounts for specific fiscal years. It does not describe any process for public comment, consultation, or advisory input.
